ABOUT THE JOB

Flatpay is on a mission to simplify payments for small and medium-sized businesses. We provide transparent, low-cost payment solutions combined with fast onboarding and real human support - fair pricing, great technology, and local support that merchants can rely on. One of the fastest-growing fintech companies out of the Nordics and Denmark's fastest-ever unicorn, we've scaled to 2,500+ colleagues across multiple markets, and we're just getting started. Pay is our terminal-only product: a card terminal, flat transparent pricing, and nothing the merchant has to configure. It is the product most of our merchants gets first, it carries the majority of our processing volume, and it is the product we lead with in every new market. This is a deliberately commercial product leadership role. Flatpay's whole model rests on a single visit: a rep walks into a bakery, a salon or a bike shop unannounced, explains flat, transparent pricing, demos the terminal, installs it and trains the staff. Everything Pay does exists to make that visit convert and to keep the merchant on the terminal afterwards. If you've only ever led product through a research team and a dashboard, this won't be the role for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own Pay end to end

• 
Own the Pay product globally - terminal hardware, the payment experience, onboarding and activation, the merchant app, settlement and reporting. One roadmap, all markets.

• 
Set the Pay strategy and defend it: what we build, what we deliberately do not build, and what stays the same across every market so the product does not fragment as we add countries.

• 
Keep the product radically simple. Our merchants are not technical and have no IT function; simplicity is the product, and protecting it is your job before it is anyone else's.

Lead the team

• 
Lead and grow the Pay product team (three PMs today, with the reporting track dotted in), setting the bar for discovery, delivery and written thinking.

• 
Be a player-coach. You'll run your own track on the hardest problems, not only review other people's.

• 
Partner with Engineering, Design and Data in Copenhagen to turn the Pay roadmap into shipped product on roughly two-month cycles, MVP mindset - get it live, learn, iterate.

The field

• 
Get out into the field. Sit with merchants, ride along with sales, spend time with support, and turn what you hear into product decisions. We expect this of a Head of Pay as much as of a PM.

• 
Partner with Sales, Support and Marketing across markets to surface what is actually happening with merchants, and feed it straight into the roadmap.

• 
Build and hold the competitive view for Pay: how competitors package and price terminal and Pay-only offers in Europe and the US, and where they are beatable.

Markets and expansion

• 
Make Pay launch-ready for each new market - acquiring setup, local payment behaviour, regulation, hardware logistics - and work with the US team in New York on what the US needs from the European product.

• 
Own outcome metrics for Pay: activation, processing volume, retention, churn, support load, and the commercial metrics above.

WHO YOU ARE

• 
3+ years in product, with experience leading product managers - and still extremely hands-on.

• 
A commercial, results-driven mindset. You think in merchants, conversion, volume and margin, and you can point to a pricing or product decision you made that moved one of them.

• 
Evidence of field-driven discovery: a decision you can name that came directly from time in front of merchants or sales, not from a research readout.

• 
A track record of shipping fast in a low-structure environment, and comfort building the structure as you go rather than waiting for it.

• 
A generalist and builder who thrives in a fast-paced scale-up and is happy working outside their comfort zone.

• 
Excellent stakeholder management across functions, markets and time zones, and excellent written and spoken English.

AI IS PART OF THE JOB

• 
Flatpay's cost advantage comes from doing things with fewer people than the incumbents. AI is how we keep that true as we add markets, and we expect a Head of Pay to treat it as part of the product, not as a side project.

• 
Use it yourself, daily. You prototype with it, you write specs and analysis with it, you run your own competitive and pricing research with it. You'll be setting the bar for three PMs, and the bar is that a PM who cannot get a working prototype or a data answer in an afternoon is slower than the role now requires.

• 
Know where it does not belong. Nothing in the authorisation path, nothing the merchant has to supervise, nothing that makes a terminal less predictable. Our merchants are not technical and have no IT function.

• 
Be honest about the economics. Inference cost, error rate and the cost of being wrong are product decisions. You should be able to argue why a model belongs in a flow at our volumes, or why a rule set is the better answer.

WHY FLATPAY?

As part of our team, you will join +2000 passionate Flatpayers dedicated to shaping the future of payments in Europe. Flatpay is proud to be a company that values diversity. We ensure an inclusive work environment for all our employees and offer opportunities for professional growth and development. We have free slushice, an on-site gym, a fully equipped gamer room, and plenty of other fun things at our office! If you are ready to be part of this exciting journey, we would love to hear from you today.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The role

You'll be the person who takes a video from idea to finished file — on your own.

Say we need a product walkthrough of a new Veo feature. Here's what that looks like for you:

• 
Plan: Set the shoot date and book the product designer who built the feature.

• 
Find the story: Interview them and write the script.

• 
Set up: Light and frame the set.

• 
Shoot: Run the shoot on our two Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6Ks and direct the person on camera.

• 
Finish: Edit, grade, mix, subtitle, and export every format we need.

Nobody hands you a shot list. Nobody needs to check in halfway.

You'll also use AI throughout your work. Some shots you'll generate in tools like Higgsfield instead of filming them. Some steps — transcripts, rough cuts, subtitles, versioning — you'll hand to AI so you can spend your time on the parts that need your eye.

You'll join Veo's Owned & Creative team in Copenhagen, working alongside graphic designers, a video producer focused on AI-generated ads, and the wider marketing team.

What you'll do

Own production end-to-end

• 
Take a brief (or spot the need yourself) and turn it into a production plan: concept, timeline, locations, people, and gear.

• 
Plan and book shoot dates with colleagues across Veo, from product designers to coaches and community members.

• 
Research the topic and interview subject-matter experts to find the story worth telling.

• 
Write scripts, talking points, and storyboards.

Run the shoot

• 
Set up the set: lighting, sound, framing, and camera settings.

• 
Operate our 2× Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6K setup, including multi-camera interviews and B-roll.

• 
Direct and interview people on camera — most of them aren't actors — so they come across confident and natural, and stick to the script when they need to.

• 
Shoot on location, in studio, and out on the pitch.

Finish the video

• 
Edit in DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro: story, pacing, color grading, sound mix, graphics, subtitles, and CTAs.

• 
Deliver multi-format versions for paid social (Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Instagram), YouTube, veo.co, and email.

• 
Organize and archive footage and finished assets in our DAM (Frontify) so the whole team can find and reuse them.

Make AI part of how you work

• 
Generate shots, B-roll, and scenes with AI video tools such as Higgsfield, and blend them with live-action footage.

• 
Use AI to speed up your workflow — automated transcripts and rough cuts, text-based editing, AI subtitles, script drafts, and fast versioning for different markets and formats.

• 
Keep testing new tools and share what works with the team.

Work with the team — without needing to be managed

• 
Align with graphic designers on art direction and brand, and with marketers on campaign goals.

• 
Manage your own pipeline, priorities, and deadlines, and flag trade-offs early.

• 
Brief and coordinate freelancers (photographers, extra crew) when a project needs them.

What we're looking for

• 
A portfolio that shows videos you've taken from idea to final cut — ideally including interview-led or product content. Please tell us what you did on each piece.

• 
3+ years of hands-on video production experience, in-house, at an agency, or freelance.

• 
Strong camera skills — confident with cinema cameras (Blackmagic experience is a plus), lighting, and recording clean audio.

• 
Strong editing skills in DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro, including color grading and sound. After Effects or motion graphics experience is a plus.

• 
You can direct people. You know how to make a nervous colleague relaxed on camera and how to interview to get a good answer.

• 
You write. You can turn an interview or a product brief into a clear script.

• 
You already use AI in your work — or you're curious and actively learning. Experience with AI video generation (e.g. Higgsfield, Runway, Kling, Veo, Sora) and AI-assisted editing is a strong plus.

• 
You're proactive and independent. You see what needs doing, make the call, and get it done. You're comfortable working without close supervision and owning the outcome.

• 
You understand performance content — what makes a viewer stop scrolling and how formats differ by channel.

• 
Fluent in English. Danish is a plus.

• 
Based in the Greater Copenhagen area.

Additional information

Before inviting candidates to interviews, we'll ask you to complete a small task. We'll only use it for the recruitment process, never commercially.

How to apply

• 
Attach your CV and a short cover letter. Tell us about a video you owned from start to finish, and how you use AI in your workflow.

• 
Include a link to your portfolio.

• 
Complete the application form.

Life at Veo

We're an office-first company. Our Copenhagen office has an indoor ball court, a rooftop terrace, and a well-equipped gym. It's built to connect people across the business, spark creative thinking, and give you space to work with colleagues, global partners, and the wider Veo community.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

Finance deserves better

Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, market or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled.

Light gives them a way out. We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one:

• 
Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one.

• 
Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting.

• 
Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter.

We take on the ERP and the legacy point solution world with something fast to implement, AI-native from the ground up, and better the more you use it.

Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée, and teams across Copenhagen, London and Stockholm, with remotes world over.

The Role

We're looking for a Nordics Marketing Manager to make Light the default finance platform for scaling companies across Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland. You can base yourself in Copenhagen or London.

Light started life in Copenhagen, and the Nordics already know us. Founders, CFOs and finance leaders in the region backed us from the start, and our local community gives us a head start most challengers would envy. Your job is to take that energy to new heights, so that when a Nordic finance team outgrows its current setup, Light is the obvious next move.

You'll own the Nordics marketing plan end to end. You'll have a B-line into our Nordics GTM pod, which spans sales, implementation and customer success, and you'll work closely with our central growth team to find new ways to drive demand through digital channels.

What you'll be doing

• 
Building and running the Nordics marketing plan, with pipeline targets you share with the GTM pod.

• 
Running a field and events programme across Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo and Helsinki and… any other city you think makes sense. From intimate CFO dinners to flagship moments people talk about for months.

• 
Growing partnerships with the accounting firms, advisors, investors and communities that Nordic finance leaders trust and extends our voice across the region.

• 
Localising our story, content and campaigns so they land with Nordic finance teams in their own language and context.

• 
Creating content with our customers, product and design teams that turns what Light does into stories people want to share.

• 
Working with our central growth team to test and scale digital demand generation in the region.

• 
Building relationships with local press and the people who shape the Nordic tech and finance conversation.

What we think* you'll need

• 
Enough years in the seat to know what works at a fast-growing company, ideally because you've built the ground game for a scaling B2B SaaS business before.

• 
A track record across field, events, partnerships and content, and the judgment to know which lever to pull and when.

• 
Experience localising a brand and its message for a region, with a feel for what lands with Nordic audiences.

• 
Comfort working with sales, implementation and customer success as one team, with pipeline as the shared goal.

• 
Deep curiosity about how AI is reshaping finance teams and the companies they serve.

• 
A great storyteller across video, text and meme.

• 
A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant assholes here, please.

• 
Fluency in English and at least one other Nordic language.

• 
A passport. Expect regular trips across the Nordics and to our teams in London, Munich, New York and elsewhere.

*If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don't tick every box, we'd still love for you to reach out and convince us you're the right person.

The Good Stuff

• 
A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in Copenhagen or London.

• 
A competitive salary and potential stock options.

• 
25 days of annual leave plus public holidays in the country where you're based.

• 
Regular socials and two company off-sites a year.

The chance to shape a category from the inside, in the region where Light began.

The Famous Last Words

The Nordics gave Light its first customers, its first champions and its first team. We want to repay that by becoming the finance platform every scaling Nordic company runs on, and we want you to lead the charge. If you know the region, love building from the ground up and want to help retire the ERP for good, let's talk.

We're looking for a Growth Marketing Manager to join our growth team and open up the channels we haven't really touched yet.

We've built a lean, efficient demand generation engine on the core paid channels you'd expect at a Series A B2B company, with Google Ads and LinkedIn doing the heavy lifting. Mercive is a digital commerce consultancy in rapid growth, scaling our brand partnerships to help define the next era of commerce. We are looking for a Director of Marketing to lead and grow our marketing department, with responsibility for strategy, new business, people and P&L.

About Mercive

We work with brands ranging from high-growth challengers to established international brands where ecommerce is a strategic driver of growth. Our offering covers technology, experience, design, operations and marketing, from strategy to implementation. Our marketing department turns our clients' commerce setup into growth and we expect to double the department next year.

The role

You will lead Mercive's marketing consultancy: a team of six specialists today across paid social, paid search, CRM and SEO, working on growth for our clients in competitive categories. The mandate is broad. You set the strategy, win the business, lead the people and own the numbers.

The department does not stand alone. Our clients come to Mercive for technology, experience and operations as well as marketing. Part of the role is to connect those offerings so that a client's growth plan, Shopify setup and daily operations are advised as one. You will define what the department should look like in two years, build the plan to get there and double the department in 2027.

Responsibilities

Strategy

• 
Set the strategy for the marketing department: offering, positioning, ways of working and how growth work is priced and packaged.

• 
Define how Mercive creates growth across paid social, paid search, CRM and SEO, keeping it current as channels, measurement and AI change what works.

• 
Connect the marketing offering to technology, experience and operations so that marketing, platform and operations are advised as one plan.

Clients and new business

• 
Lead pitches and proposals for marketing engagements, for new clients and across Mercive's existing client base.

• 
Act as the senior advisor on growth for the brands we work with: understand their business, challenge their plans and tie marketing investment to commercial results.

• 
Build and maintain the department's pipeline together with Mercive's leadership team.

Leadership

• 
Lead and develop the current team of six, with clear roles, priorities and standards for advice and delivery.

• 
Define the future team and hire it: roles, seniority and sequence for doubling the department in 2027.

• 
Build a consultancy culture in the department: senior advice, measurable outcomes and quality in every deliverable.

P&L

• 
Own the department's P&L: revenue, margin, pricing, utilisation and forecasting.

• 
Plan capacity against pipeline and report on the department's performance.

Who you are

You have strong business acumen and a clear view of what drives growth in the new digital era. You can lead a conversation with a founder, CMO or ecommerce director about their business, not only their channels. You understand the importance of combining business and digital commerce in the advice you give. We expect that you:

• 
Have led a marketing or performance team in an agency, consultancy or brand, with responsibility for results and budget.

• 
Know paid social, paid search, CRM and SEO well enough to set direction for specialists and judge the quality of their work, without needing to run the campaigns yourself.

• 
Have pitched and won business and are comfortable as the senior face of a proposal.

• 
Have owned or co-owned a P&L and can read a department's economics.

• 
Have built or grown a team and can describe how you would define the next one.

• 
Understand commerce and how marketing, platform and operations depend on each other.

• 
Work fluently in Danish and English.

What we offer

• 
A director role with a real mandate: the department's strategy, team, clients and P&L are yours.

• 
The rest of Mercive behind you across technology, experience, design and operations, so that your advice is backed by the ability to implement it.

• 
Clients among Nordic scale and enterprise brands, most of them on Shopify.

• 
A consultancy of around 30 people with a short distance from decision to action and a leadership team who are close to the work.

• 
Salary and terms that match the responsibility.

Practical

The role is based at our office at Strandgade 56 in Copenhagen. The preferred start date is 4 January 2027. We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the position when we have found the right person. Send your CV and a cover letter explaining why you are the right fit.

Oxfam is one of the world’s largest development and humanitarian organisations, and our analyses and messages are heard by global leaders and in the Danish debate. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Positions in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The research group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two Postdoctoral Researcher positions in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics.

  Professor Mikkelsen’s group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group’s experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI’s new building. Postdocs joining now will help build the laboratory and shape its first experiments. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

  The positions span three axes of control over light–matter interaction; the balance between them will depend on the candidates:

  Spatial structure — shaping the vacuum around an emitter and concentrating the field for nonlinear optics, with examples including Purcell tensors, the nanophotonic Lamb shift, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients.

  Emitter number — cavity QED with exactly one, two or several emitters, including the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and multi-exciton emission that outruns Auger recombination.

  Temporal control — ultrafast and time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, optically dressed states in quantum materials embedded in nanogaps, and time-varying cavities.

  We seek outstanding, creative, and highly motivated experimentalists with a PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, and a strong background in one or more of: nanophotonics or cavity QED; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic spectroscopy of solid-state emitters or two-dimensional materials; ultrafast optical spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Candidates are encouraged to propose directions of their own within this scope; the programme will be shaped by the people who join.

  The successful candidates will carry out experimental research, help set up the new laboratory, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet, a tunable femtosecond laser system and single-photon confocal spectroscopy, publish and present results, and participate in the supervision of students. The positions may also include collaboration with national and international research partners and other academic duties as required. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

   

  Further information on the Department at https://nbi.ku.dk/english/. Informal inquiries are welcome and can be made to Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The positions are for three years, starting as soon as possible, with flexible start dates into 2027.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

jobs.description:
The Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a fixed-term Assistant Professor position in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics, in the group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen. The position is for four years, open from as soon as possible; a later start in 2027 can be negotiated.

Professor Mikkelsen's group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk second-order nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group's experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI's new building. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

The Assistant Professor will lead an independent research direction within the group’s programme on light–matter interaction in nanocavities. Directions of particular interest include:

• 
Cavity QED with few emitters — strong coupling with exactly one, two or several quantum emitters in deterministically fabricated nanogaps, the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and quantum light generation from nanocavity-coupled emitters

• 
Quantum and two-dimensional materials in nanogaps — out-of-plane excitations (interlayer excitons, dark excitons, trions) coupled to the vertical field of a nanogap at cryogenic temperatures and in vector magnetic fields; optically dressed states of 2D semiconductors and magnets driven inside a nanogap and read out by single-cavity ultrafast spectroscopy

• 
Ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics — time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, time-varying cavities, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients

 Candidates are expected to define their own experimental programme within this scope, and proposals that cut across these directions are welcome.

This is a leadership position for an early-career scientist ready for independence. The Assistant Professor will be the senior scientist in the group alongside Professor Mikkelsen, with day-to-day responsibility for one research direction and its students. The successful candidate will take scientific ownership of the group's new cryogenic and ultrafast facilities, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet and a tunable femtosecond laser system, co-supervise PhD and master's students, and develop their own funding portfolio, with active support from the group and the institute. They will be supported in applying as principal investigator for Danish and European early-career grants, and the position includes a dedicated budget line for a student and consumables. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

We seek an outstanding experimentalist, typically three to seven years after the PhD, with a strong publication record, demonstrated independence, and hands-on expertise in several of: nanophotonics, cavity QED or plasmonics; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy; ultrafast pump–probe spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Expertise in the exfoliation, transfer, assembly and encapsulation of van der Waals heterostructures, including gated devices, is an asset. Experience supervising students and an interest in teaching are expected. The group is simultaneously recruiting postdoctoral researchers; candidates may apply to both positions.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, funded by external research grants, and is not tenure-track. The objective is that the successful candidate concludes the appointment with an established research direction, an independent funding record, and a strong case for a permanent position at the University of Copenhagen or elsewhere.

The assistant professor’s duties will primarily include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within quantum optics and photonics. To a limited extent this may also include performance of other duties. 

Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.
